title: Add opaque residency proxy and operator RBAC throttle
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: Operators and cross-service tooling can amplify residency and KMS risk if delegated credentials are used without a residency-aware guard. This PR introduces an Opaque Residency Proxy (ORP) that centralizes residency-assertion verification, attaches region-bound residency proofs to downstream requests, and enforces KMS usage locality. It also adds an RBACv2 'operator throttle' layer that rate-limits and time-bounds delegated operator grants to reduce lateral blast radius. The change is intended for customers using Private and Dedicated deployments to strengthen data-residency guarantees and auditability while minimizing false positives for normal control-plane operations. Implementation summary: 1) New service components: ORP service (go) and ORP-enforcer sidecar (small wasm filter) that validates incoming operator claims against the residency policy engine and requests a short-lived residency proof token from the KMS-assertor. 2) KMS integration: extended kmspolicy client to support region-anchored key wraps and an 'assert-and-wrap' call that emits a signed residency-proof header (residency-proof:v1) bound to the key manifest and operator claim. 3) RBACv2 extension: operator_throttle policy type and enforcement hook in the policy-evaluator to apply per-operator ephemeral grant limits and cooldown windows. 4) Audit: audit-proxy now accepts an opaque provenance envelope that contains residency-proof metadata and a hash of the original operator token; the envelope is signed and stored in the immutable audit store while PII fields are redacted. 5) Migration: dual-write to audit-v1 and audit-v2 during the rollout; ORP runs in permissive mode by default and flips to enforce after telemetry validation. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and security review (ENG-4219) - [x] Unit tests for ORP and kmspolicy client - [x] Integration test harness for operator_throttle behavior - [x] e2e smoke in staging with permissive mode - [x] Gradual rollout plan with canary and telemetry gating - [x] Docs: operator/residency and KMS integration pages Notes: This description intentionally avoids including raw token samples. See design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4219 for full diagrams and threat model.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial ORP scaffold; add kmspolicy assert-and-wrap client; wasm sidecar filter for ORP enforcement; rbacv2 operator_throttle policy and evaluator hook; audit envelope writer and retention test; helper refactors and small lint fixes.

infra/wasm/orp_filter.rs - wasm filter for incoming operator claims
policy/evaluator/operator_throttle.go - new policy type and enforcement
review_comments: Evan Park: Can we ensure the ORP handles clock skew between regions? Suggest adding monotonic TTL checks on residency proofs.
Priya (author): Added monotonic TTL validation and a clock-drift tolerance flag (configurable by region) in the latest patch.
Lena Ortiz: Audit envelope needs to be searchable for compliance queries. Can we keep an indexed minimal fingerprint?
Priya (author): We add a canonical fingerprint (sha256) to the envelope metadata and index it in the compliance table; value is non-PII.
Arjun Patel: How does this affect Dedicated customers using external KMS providers?

Priya (author): ORP supports a KMS-provider adapter interface; we ship adapters for AWS and GCP. For external KMS we fall back to a blinded-assertor path that records provider provenance without exporting raw keys.
Evan Park: CI flaked once on the wasm build, re-run passed.
Lena Ortiz: Approve after a small doc tweak.
QA: Verified operator_throttle cooldown in staging under simulated burst; no false denies observed.
Security: Completed threat model and pen-test smoke; approved with low/medium mitigations logged.
merge_outcome: merged on 2026-03-02 via squash and merge. Merge commit message: 'feature: ORP residency proxy + operator RBAC throttle (ENG-4219)'. Release note drafted and attached.
release_notes: Added Opaque Residency Proxy (ORP) to validate residency assertions and emit region-bound residency proofs; Introduced operator_throttle RBACv2 policy to limit delegated operator grants and reduce lateral risk; Extended kmspolicy client with assert-and-wrap to produce residency-proof headers; Audit pipeline now supports signed opaque envelopes with PII redaction and indexed fingerprints; Rollout is staged with permissive default and telemetry gating.
security_impact: Improves residency enforcement for KMS operations and reduces operator lateral movement risk. Adds new indexed fingerprints to audit store (non-PII). Requires operators of private deployments to update agent images to include ORP sidecar; older agents will run in permissive mode and receive telemetry warnings.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy ORP in staging behind routing flag; 2) Run in permissive mode for 2 weeks and collect telemetry; 3) Enable operator_throttle in canary (1% traffic) and monitor denies; 4) Ramp to 25% if denies are negligible; 5) Flip ORP to enforce after SLOs validated; 6) Offer emergency opt-out per-tenant for 72h through support ticket while we investigate.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests added for kmspolicy AssertAndWrap and operator_throttle evaluator. Integration harness simulates cross-region operator bursts and verifies cooldown windows. Staging e2e executed with permissive mode; QA load test validated audit envelope throughput under 10k r/s while maintaining <150ms median extra latency.
migration_steps: 1) Ship ORP and kmspolicy clients; 2) Dual-write audit envelopes (v1 + v2) for 30 days; 3) Run compliance queries to validate indexed fingerprints; 4) Notify Dedicated/Private customers about agent image update requirement and provide migration guide; 5) After 30 days, switch to single audit-v2 storage once verified.
notes: This PR purposely implements minimal surface area in the core policy-evaluator and keeps operator_throttle as an opt-in policy that tenants can enable via policy bundles. The ORP is pluggable and intended to host additional residency heuristics later (e.g., workload tagging).
